classification.difficultyReason: Apply the external-secant product rule, distinguishing whole secant lengths from their internal portions.

content.prompt: $PQ$ and $TS$ are two secants of a circle intersecting externally at $R$. Given that $PQ=5\text{ cm}$, $QR=7\text{ cm}$ and $SR=4\text{ cm}$, find the length of $TS$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5 diagram, right of the stem
spec.description: Unshaded circle with external point R on the right. Upper secant has order P–Q–R; lower secant has order T–S–R. Ordinary source blue strokes are reconstructed in house black.
spec.mathematics: Both secants meet the same external point R. P, Q, S and T lie on the circle; Q and S are the nearer intersections.
spec.answerVisibility: No answers or additional numerical labels appear in the question diagram.

answer.worked:
Using secants from an external point,
$$\begin{align*}
RQ\times RP&=RS\times RT\\
7(7+5)&=4(4+TS)\\
84&=16+4TS\\
4TS&=68\\
TS&=17\text{ cm}.
\end{align*}$$
